title: The Winter's Tale (Part 1)
description: The lesson that closes the unit: read a tale and hand it back in five lines. What a narrative text is for (to entertain, to tell a story, to give a literary pleasure) and how it is built - the four windows a reader looks through (setting, characters, plot, theme, and why the theme is not the plot), the kinds of narrative (imaginary, factual or a mixture; fable, myth, historical narrative, slice of life and the rest), and the five stages of a plot (introduction, problem, climax or crisis, resolution, conclusion). Then a real tale, Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale as Charles and Mary Lamb retold it in prose: reading it twice, once for the people and the ties between them and once for the notes (Characters | Action, hunt the main verbs), and turning those notes into a five-line summary that keeps the order and one tense, leaves out description, dialogue and opinion, and links its sentences with connectors of time. The grammar comes out of the tale itself: so + adjective + that, which says how far something went and what came of it, against the other jobs of the little word so
